header_summary:
The Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) 300 is currently vulnerable to manipulation by attackers who can influence bundle scores through ALARM messages, potentially allowing an attacker with a 26% stake to censor BIP 300 bundles indefinitely. Proposed changes include banning ALARM messages and other downvoting mechanisms to reinforce the security model back to a 75% honest majority assumption, thus aligning more closely with Bitcoin's standard of a 50% honest majority. These adjustments aim to enhance the integrity and fairness of the drivechain process, essential for secure Bitcoin transactions. [More details](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/2e554c89-a2a1-4bcf-941c-32f6a8ba9567n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#m8c5a1483ce116d2f2cd883a2f4e160fc93a6bd03).

In parallel, advancements in Bitcoin's payment infrastructure are being driven by protocols like [Intents](https://docs.arkadeos.com/intents/overview), [Kaleidoswap](https://kaleidoswap.com/), and [Cassis](https://cassis.cash/), which facilitate seamless transactions across multiple layers using Hash Time Locked Contracts (HTLCs). The Cassis system, particularly, allows for offline fund reception and offers users the flexibility to balance privacy, security, and custody by selecting appropriate layers. However, the implementation, still in progress, faces challenges such as establishing a reliable reputation system for routing nodes and enhancing communication protocols. [Read more](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/cassis-a-new-simple-scheme-for-generic-multi-layer-multi-hop-htlc-routing/2952).

recent_posts.title: RE BIP 300: 26% censoring attack
recent_posts.summary:
- Security risks in BIP 300 arise from score manipulation via ALARM messages.
- Proposed changes eliminate downvoting to uphold a 51% success threshold.
- Enhancements aim to strengthen drivechain process and ensure transaction security.

recent_posts.title: Cassis, a new simple scheme for generic multi-layer multi-hop HTLC routing
recent_posts.summary: - Bitcoin's evolving payment landscape is boosted by initiatives like Arkade, Kaleidoswap, and Cassis.  - Cassis enables indirect payment chains for Bitcoin, improving settlement, costs, and offline transactions.  - Technical challenges remain, including standardizing node communication and securing fund reclamation.

active_posts.title: Flame: confidential transactions with Bitcoin proof-of-burn consensus
active_posts.summary:
- The Flame project introduces a Bitcoin side chain using a proof-of-burn mechanism.
- It features Bulletproofs, Ristretto, and Taproot to ensure transaction security and privacy.
- Flame's mainnet launch is planned for January 2027 to enhance decentralized applications.

active_posts.title: Lichen: L2s In CHannels ENforced on bitcoin
active_posts.summary:
- This L2 transaction system keeps user-hub contracts secure without needing trust in hub honesty.
- Disputes are resolved efficiently with on-chain RISC Zero and Groth16 cryptographic proofs.
- The central hub model risks centralization but secures transactions with backed reserve tokens.

active_posts.title: [bitcoindev]
active_posts.summary:
- Luke Carriere's email discusses standardizing blockchain security enforcement policies.
- The draft aims for interoperability among blockchain services using a unified policy format.
- Feedback is requested on unresolved aspects of the policy draft format and structure.

active_posts.title: Disclosure: DoS vulnerabilities fixed in Eclair v0.14.1
active_posts.summary:
- Eclair's version 0.14.1 update fixes two critical security vulnerabilities.
- The first flaw involves a DoS vulnerability that could severely affect memory management.
- The second vulnerability allows attackers to create unfunded channels and crash nodes.

active_posts.title: Anchoring an SPV light client on another chain: checkpoint trust, retargeting and reorg handling
active_posts.summary:
- The Writz Protocol uses Bitcoin as collateral and issues loans in USDC on Stellar.
- It features security scripts for Bitcoin and strict verification via SPV client model.
- Areas highlighted for improvement include trust points and transaction fee management.

active_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
active_posts.summary:
- Luke Carriere's draft proposes a standardized policy format for co-signer transactions.
- It includes varying verification processes to ensure secure co-signing conditions.
- The draft seeks feedback on key aspects to refine its practicality and effectiveness.

today_in_history_posts.title: Bitcoin Archaeology
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The author seeks to replicate early Bitcoin versions with original build tools.  - Challenges include obsolete software and a specific script bug in OpenSSL.  - Multiple solutions are considered, including finding old compilers or using newer tools.

today_in_history_posts.title: [RFC] Simplified (but less optimal) HTLC Negotiation
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Lightning Labs found another insufficiency in the specification despite an optimal HTLC state machine.
- A new protocol has been introduced, streamlining processes with deterministic fee changes and fewer transactions.
- This protocol operates half-duplex, adding one RTT latency if it's not your turn to communicate.

today_in_history_posts.title: CVE-2024-38365 public disclosure (btcd `FindAndDelete` bug)
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Niklas Gögge and Antoine Poinsot identified a critical flaw in old Btcd software.
- They reported the issue, leading to a bug bounty and software corrections.
- The vulnerability was fully addressed and disclosed by September 20, 2024.
